contract_md:
- **POST-1** Input contains an integer pair \(N,Q\), one row of \(N\) integers \(A_i\), and \(Q\) query rows containing integer pairs \(R_i,X_i\). The bounds are \(1\le N,Q\le 200000\), \(1\le A_i\le 10^9\), \(1\le R_i\le N\), and \(\min(A_1,\ldots,A_{R_i})\le X_i\le 10^9\).
- **POST-2** Output contains exactly \(Q\) lines with one decimal integer per line, in the original query order.
- **POST-3** The answer to \((R,X)\) is the maximum \(k\) for which there are indices \(1\le j_1<\cdots<j_k\le R\) with \(A_{j_1}<\cdots<A_{j_k}\) and every selected value at most \(X\). An element equal to \(X\) is eligible. Repeated values cannot both occur in a strictly increasing subsequence.
- **POST-4** Every answer is at least one and at most the number of distinct eligible values in the prefix. It is one for a singleton prefix, a nonincreasing prefix, or a threshold equal to the prefix minimum.
- **POST-5** Identical queries have identical answers. Increasing \(R\) or \(X\) while holding the other fixed cannot decrease the answer. An increase of \(d\) in either coordinate alone raises the answer by at most \(d\). Preserving the order and all value comparisons among eligible elements preserves the answer.
- **POST-6** A Python 3 submission must handle simultaneous maximum values of \(N\) and \(Q\). Quadratic work or storage in \(N\) or \(Q\), or worst-case work proportional to \(NQ\), is incompatible with these limits.

isolation.mechanism: hardened isolated codex exec (empty tmpdir, read-only, tool flags disabled, credentials stripped, full event-lifecycle audit including item.started)
